description: Meeting recovery workflow for declined one-on-one meetings that identifies candidates, proposes slots, creates Outlook drafts, and delivers results via Teams/email. NOTE : If JSON upload isn't supported, copy the JSON content and paste it into the Scout Cloud prompt to set up the automation.
condition: A newly declined one-on-one meeting is detected in my calendar or inbox responses.
name: Reschedule Declined 1:1

steps.label: Collect recent decline signals
steps.prompt:
Review recent calendar responses and meeting-related emails since the last run. Identify decline actions tied to meeting invitations from BOTH sides: (a) user declined someone else’s invite, and (b) another participant declined a user-organized invite.

Detection requirements (do all):
1) Pull recent mailbox items using workiq_list_emails with Graph select fields that include meeting-response metadata (for example meetingMessageType/messageClass equivalents where available), not only keyword search.
2) Treat explicit meeting-decline response messages as decline signals even when the subject does NOT start with 'Declined:' and even when decline text appears only in the body (e.g., '<name> declined'). For such candidates, call workiq_get_email to inspect full body when preview is insufficient.
3) Correlate with calendar events (workiq_list_events) and attendee statuses to capture organizer-side declines from counterparts.
4) Exclude automation summary/status emails (e.g., 'Declined 1:1 Recovery Run Summary') and exclude organizer-cancelled meetings unless there is an explicit attendee decline signal.

Return a deduplicated candidate list with: event/message id, subject, direction (user-declined vs counterpart-declined), and evidence source (meeting-response email body, meetingMessageType/messageClass, attendee status).

steps.label: Filter to valid 1:1 candidates
steps.prompt: Keep only meetings that are true one-on-one sessions (organizer + one attendee), excluding room/resource-only scenarios and group meetings. Accept candidates whether the decline came from the user or the other participant.

steps.label: Build meeting context
steps.prompt: For each declined 1:1, capture key context: subject, organizer, attendee, who declined (user or counterpart), original date/time, duration, timezone, and whether this appears to be a recurring series.

steps.label: Resolve participants and constraints
steps.prompt: Resolve both participants to canonical identities and gather scheduling constraints including working hours, conflicts, and out-of-office blocks.

steps.label: Generate recovery options
steps.prompt: Find the best 3 replacement slots within the next 7 business days that fit both calendars, preserving original duration and timezone when possible. Rank by earliest viable and minimal disruption.

steps.label: Create Outlook Drafts
steps.prompt: For each declined 1:1 with valid replacement options, create a real Outlook draft (not just text output) using workiq_create_draft. Address it to the counterpart participant (the non-user participant), keep tone concise and professional, include exactly the top 3 proposed slots with timezone and original duration, and ask for preferred option. Return each created draft ID and subject.

steps.label: Deliver summary via Teams/email
steps.prompt: After draft creation, deliver the run result through a user-visible channel instead of output-only text: (1) send a Teams self-chat summary using workiq_get_my_profile + workiq_create_chat_by_email + workiq_send_chat_message, and (2) send an email summary to the user mailbox with workiq_send_email. Include per meeting: subject, original time, 3 proposed slots, and the created Outlook draft SUBJECT only (do NOT include draft ID). If no candidates are found, still send a concise 'no action needed' notification through both channels.
